family_assessments.assessment: The intended task was to reconstruct the trustee roster at a bank-meeting cut-off despite signed papers and later administration. The blind review verified that registered release effects simultaneous retirement and replacement, while an affirmative hold through the cut-off preserves the incumbent (family_a/review/blind-review.md). Fresh excerpt review verified the joint route through the operative instrument and custodian disposition and rejected a proposed shorter route (family_a/review/necessity.md). A0/A1 preserve the key and ordinary context under an order-only change (family_a/review/matched-sources.json). The bank and administrative material also contains supported kinship and irrelevant operational detail; neither is separately controlled. Latest-note or name-frequency shortcuts favour the incumbent, while promoting signed draft material favours the successor. Retain the bounded two-person office contrast; it does not generalise to silent custody records or other effectiveness rules.
family_assessments.overlap: Shares joint proof with B and C and the reading of operative instruments with D. A changes whether an act takes effect; D changes what an already effective act reaches.

family_assessments.assessment: The intended task was to identify the speaker of a parentage report without guessing from the contact list. The comparison verified that an independently maintained session record binds the native statement to one named speaker only when the field is complete (family_b/review/outputs/comparison.json). The incomplete field leaves two compatible speakers, and both readings retain the ordinary parent edge (family_b/review/agreement.json). The native export and relay share an informant; forward-only readings do not fix attribution (family_b/review/mask-results.json). Identity or statement deletions defeated the target without removing unaffected kinship (family_b/review/proof-deletions.json). The clerk's original-document sighting is useful independent context, not the attribution mechanism. A completeness check followed by choosing the first contact can reproduce the graph delta. Retain; do not credit the graph alone as proof of attribution or treat the relay as corroboration.
family_assessments.overlap: Like C, B withholds a named edge when an identifier is incomplete, but B identifies a speaker, not a trust. F retains complete identity evidence. B establishes common origin, not the effect of increasing repetition or adding an independent contradiction.

family_assessments.assessment: The intended task was to map an operative designation to one of two settlements through a separately held custody reference. The comparison verified that switching the parent-deed reference switches the trust endpoint and that both allocations remain viable when the distinguishing character is obscured (family_c/review/outputs/comparison.json). Independent excerpt readers verified a three-Source proof; whole-file masks defeat the target while preserving ten ordinary edges (family_c/review/proof-deletions.json). Both readers withheld both candidate endpoints in the partial-reference condition (family_c/review/agreement.json). Fixed-trust, first-trust and assign-both rules fail across conditions. Shared trustees, a wish letter, expenses and meeting details add documentary texture, but one register entry and two parallel settlements limit the inference. Retain the join and invariant-graph check without crediting a separate distraction or volume effect.
family_assessments.overlap: Shares joint proof with A and B and restraint under incomplete information with B. C selects between two established trusts; D changes the reach of a provision within one trust.

family_assessments.assessment: The approved scoped-trust-amendment revision 1 predicted that changing only the provision locator would switch the earlier survivor while fixing the replacement, trust and unaffected relationships. The coverage register's D matched-control and closing-audit observations support that prediction: D0/D1 differ only in the operative locator, the replacement and unrelated relationships persist, and grouped scope proof was independently verified for the current beneficiary edges. The packet does not establish completion of every individual fact deletion. The separate office and beneficiary provisions and the signed variation's effective date add context; neither chronology nor unrelated kinship is independently tested. The locator alone can predict the graph without supplying the necessary proof. Retain this specific scope contrast and refine individual deletion checks in future work without changing the admitted key.
family_assessments.overlap: A tests whether an act became effective; D holds that fixed and changes the provision reached. It shares C's joint-proof discipline but does not resolve a trust endpoint.

family_assessments.assessment: The approved complete-record-label-collision revision 1 predicted exact graph and proof invariance when one ancillary display label becomes nonunique but authoritative identities and links remain complete. The coverage register's F matched-control and mask observations support that prediction: F0/F1 differ only in one populated label, both complete named graphs and their separately attached proof sets persist, and withholding the exact identity entry defeats its dependent named edge. In the isolated excerpt review, one reader entered a different structured surname despite identifying the intended person in prose; an independent repeat on the identical packet returned the correct surname. This is a documented coding discrepancy, not evidence of a systematic effect. Positional pairing still reproduces the graph. Retain the bounded display-label control; don't extend it to collisions in authoritative identifiers.
family_assessments.overlap: B makes speaker attribution incomplete; F leaves identity resolution possible in both conditions. Like C, F checks graph and proof invariance, but its intervention changes an ancillary label rather than the support for a target edge.

gaps.finding: B verifies one origin and its relay, not independent conflict or the effect of repetition. E revision 3 and W revision 2 are technically qualified but not admitted; earlier E conditions remain diagnostic only. Do not credit them as admitted solutions to same-scope disagreement or infer a priority rule from recency.

D verifies one express scoped substitution and grouped proof, not full individual fact-level necessity or other amendment mechanisms. N revision 3 and O revision 7 add qualified coverage rather than admitted controls. A correct roster with a locator, title entry or other insufficient attachment remains a distinct error.

B, C and F provide different bounded identity or endpoint checks, not interacting gaps or collisions in authoritative identifiers. A supplies the admitted order-only contrast; other natural file orders and review permutations do not amount to independent matched controls.

C establishes a substantial invariant graph and X is qualified for an incidental-support intervention, not for burial, placement or volume. The admitted evidence does not separately test settling property versus remitting funds, or whether an actual asset movement between continuing trusts licenses any transfer of personal relationships.

T is qualified for supplied-record inspection scope at the intermediate tier, not for acquisition or an interaction effect. A separately interpretable missing-original or interacting-authority test would need its own design. Retrieval, OCR, physical recovery and claims about practitioner prevalence require a scope change; longer files alone do not test them.

result.portfolio_summary: The five formally admitted Matter histories are A, B, C, D and F. Count each once, regardless of its number of conditions. The strongest repeated coverage is exact, jointly sufficient evidence on the same edge. Identity and withholding recur, but B tests speaker attribution, C tests the trust endpoint, and F tests invariance under a non-authoritative label collision. A isolates effectiveness at a cut-off; D isolates the scope of an amendment whose effectiveness is fixed. Documentary variety in these files does not establish a workload effect. Six further histories are reported as technically qualified, not admitted: X for incidental firsthand correspondence and T for bounded inspection in a 25-Source handover both await human admission; N revision 3, E revision 3, W revision 2 and O revision 7 are newly technically qualified for counterpart execution, contradictory parent reports, competing trustee accounts and title-application progress with fixed office, respectively. E's earlier returned conditions remain diagnostic only. The packet does not establish completion of the 19-history pre-giant goal. The intermediate and large tiers are separate commitments; there are no paid extraction observations or sealed evaluation results. Rank BF first for an underused settlor decision in a routine closing file, and BG second for distinguishing an actual asset transfer from changes in named relationships across continuing trusts. Both are reserves, not commissions. Neither needs a manufactured sibling; stop at two rather than add a near-duplicate.

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers independently read the operative and reconciliation views before testing exact joint excerpts. Test the extract, allocation, funding instruction, completion minute and banking trail alone and in the strongest shorter combinations. Distinguish an instruction to provide property from an attestation of completed settlement.

Delete necessary linkage and attribution facts separately, including duplicates, and independently reconstruct full diagnostic keys. Record both the strongest exact evidence for the settlor and the positive documentary basis for excluding the payment-only route. Credit any genuine alternative subset; return the proposed design if the allocation distinction is dispensable.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The named settlor edge is supported on the intact file; the remitter's documented handling and cost payment provide no other settlor edge. Exact passages should identify the operative allocation, its completed settlement entry and the named person. Removing a required fact defeats the route that uses it; loss of the edge follows only if no other sufficient route survives.
genres_and_provenance: Executed settlement extract retained in the trustees' operative file: identifies the trust, establishes ordinary provisions and gives the signed closing allocation its stated function.
Contributor's signed funding instruction retained on the closing file: records authority to use the specified money for settlement without independently attesting to completed constitution.
Remitter's native instruction retained by the closing team: states from direct knowledge which portion is handled on another person's behalf and which is for the remitter's costs.
Bank credit advice retained by the receiving finance team: records the posted aggregate payment and remitting account.
Signed completion allocation retained with the operative papers: records the authorised closing sign-off, allocation of the posted funds and the person settling the property.
Fee note retained with the accounts: identifies the charge and customer for the non-settlement item.
Trustees' dated closing minute retained in the governance file: records completion checks and the first administration tasks without purporting to replace the signed allocation.
Dated adviser brief retained on the advice file: sets the post-closing cut-off and separates the relationship question from payment reconciliation.
design.intervention: Score one intact natural file. In review only, remove the exact fact linking the signed allocation to the operative extract, then separately remove the allocation's settled-property attribution and any copies of it. Mask the bank advice and fee note separately as administrative controls. Rederive each full key before judging any removal.
invariants: The underlying transaction, exact names, trust, completed closing chronology and review cut-off are fixed.
The independent ordinary trust relationships retain sufficient proof under target-only diagnostics. A payment record does not change capacity when another Source is masked.
negative_controls: The remitter's name is affirmatively supported in the bank and cost views, but the exact apportionment and operative scope distinguish those roles from settling property. This is not a negative relationship predicate.
An unrelated trust relationship survives all focal deletions. If independently documented completion makes the bank posting unnecessary to the graph proof, the bank mask must preserve the key.
design.scenario: The practitioner has two genuine closing tasks: confirm the constitution recorded in the settlement papers and account for the combined incoming payment. Different records establish the remitter, the cost payer and the person identified as settling the property. The cash trail is useful without being an independent declaration of the relationship.
shortcut_heuristics: Check largest-payment, bank-account-holder, fee-payer, all-signers and name-frequency rules. Inspect headings, file positions, filenames and summaries for a leaked roster or mechanical row pairing.
Audit who originates each instruction, allocation and payment fact. A minute copied into an advice note does not become an independent closing finding.
success_criteria: Two isolated readers of every Source independently recover the same complete exact-name graph. Fresh excerpt and removal readers agree on sufficient same-edge proof, the precise limit of the remittance record and what each deletion leaves open.

Stop if the combined payment or adopted allocation is not natural, required ordinary records would duplicate the decisive relationship, or identifying the settlor requires tracing beneficial ownership or applying unstated law.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and closing reconciliation 10–15; blind full-file and fresh excerpt or removal review 9–14; adjudication and audit 7–11; owner realism and readiness review 2–4. Assumes one closing, two isolated full-file readers and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 8 natural Sources. Operative, participant, banking, accounting and governance records each have a distinct closing purpose; do not split a single ordinary document merely to meet the count.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse A's operative proof checks, C's independently rederived diagnostic keys, and the existing exact-passage and same-edge sufficiency checks.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use settlor_of and the independently supported ordinary Person/Trust predicates. Remittance, fees, money held on behalf and administrative capacities belong in the companion register. No asset, account or organisation node is scored.
risks_and_limits: A complete natural closing pack may provide a shorter independently sufficient route. Credit it in review and return the design if it removes the scientific distinction; do not suppress the record.
One closing does not establish who would be treated as a settlor under real law or how often payment and settlement capacities differ.

assumptions: The executed fictional terms and the expressly adopted, signed and completed allocation affirmatively identify who settles the initial property. Routing, cost payment and inferred economic ownership are not substitutes for that identification.

A disclosed arrangement for collecting a single remittance and allocating it to distinct purposes is credible for the retainer. Both participants know and report only their own instructions or actions. The proposed inventory is a workload assumption, not an estimate of practice.
The freeze cut-off is after agreed completion, posting and receipt of the papers, but at the first review of the closing material. Include any substantive closing record ordinarily available then.
grounding.documentary_situation: A participant transmits a combined amount covering settlement money they handle on another person's behalf and a separately funded cost item. The executed papers identify the signed closing allocation as the record of who is settling the initial property. The completed allocation identifies that person and separates the cost item. Bank and fee records account for what moved and why; they do not name a settlor by virtue of payment.
grounding.legal_workflow: Close the initial funding of an executed settlement, reconcile a combined remittance, and verify the closing papers before the first trust administration briefing.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Identify the named settlor and ordinary trust relationships at the first post-closing review, separately from who transmitted funds or met costs.
practitioner_unknowns: Would the adviser naturally retain a separately signed closing allocation that the executed instrument adopts, rather than identify every settlor conclusively in the principal text?
Would this closing and billing arrangement permit a combined remittance and leave a credible, separately reconciled record of the two purposes?

references.relevance: Grounds the retention of instruments, expense records and payment records, not an incorporated closing allocation, the use of a combined remittance or the legal identity of a settlor.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Settlement closing and reconciliation of the initial trust property and separately billed establishment costs.

objective.coverage_gap: AQ can distinguish a personal officeholder from a signer acting for a corporate trustee, but it cannot diagnose role attribution across different portions of one cash movement. O separates filing progress from an independently fixed office; neither O nor AQ identifies a named settlor through the executed file's distinction between settlement property and costs.
objective.failure_mechanism: A system may assign settlor status to the account holder who sent the funds, treat payment of a fee as contributing trust property, or give the correct name with only a bank or ledger citation.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: The closed file supports a named settlor through the executed settlement and its completed allocation, not through remittance or fee payment. Exact recovery of the complete graph with a sufficient attached subset disconfirms the predicted errors on this file. Reject the design if the financial records must be treated as conferring the role or an ordinarily retained record bypasses the allocation distinction.

proposals.title: The person remitting the closing funds is not necessarily the settlor

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers reconstruct the transfer and governance views separately, then test exact passages for each trust and current provision, the transfer's limiting language and the designation's independent effect. Test whether the designation or a verified extract alone is sufficient and do not demand irrelevant accounting citations.

Independently rederive the complete graph for each proper deletion, including all copies of the deleted fact. Search accounts, side letters, receiving schedules and summaries for alternate named routes. Verify route necessity separately from edge necessity and attach evidence for the correct trust on each edge.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The complete graph includes the separately licensed overlap as two edges with distinct trust endpoints, and no receiving edge sourced only to asset movement. A proper deletion on one trust side defeats only the affected route, not the other trust's edge. An exact graph with transfer material attached instead of a sufficient operative route fails the proof check.
genres_and_provenance: Verified source-trust operative extract retained by its trustees: identifies the trust and its standing named provisions relevant to the review.
Verified receiving-trust operative extract retained by its trustees: identifies the distinct trust, an ordinary continuing relationship and the authority for the separate designation.
Executed asset transfer instrument retained in both governance files: records the specific asset scope, both settlements and the limits of what the transaction changes.
Outgoing provider's dated transfer-out advice retained with the source trust's investments: identifies the released holdings and booking.
Receiving provider's dated receipt advice retained with the destination investments: identifies the posted receipt from its own books without confirming any relationship.
Receiving trustees' dated signed designation retained in their decision file: records the independent named provision and its effective terms.
Accountant's cross-account reconciliation retained with the period-close work: matches the provider entries and explains any booking differences without resolving current provisions.
Dated adviser briefing note retained on the advice file: defines the two review questions and fixes the cut-off without giving a roster.
design.intervention: Score one intact natural file. In review only, properly delete the receiving designation's focal named assertion and all copies; separately remove the source trust assertion for the same overlapping person. Mask the provider records and reconciliation as a group to test whether the relationship key survives. Do not score any mask as a sibling.
invariants: Maintain two exact trust identities, the actual asset movement, the operative chronology and one dated cut-off in the full file.

Source-only and other ordinary relationships retain their own evidence in target-only removals. The independently effective designation does not become dependent on movement merely because both records are retained together.
negative_controls: The signed transfer's exact scope gives affirmative evidence that it does not make the receiving designation or adopt the source provisions. It does not disprove any relationship supported through a separate act.

The two provider advices show real movement, not a proposed or failed transaction. Removing the accounting evidence should leave the licensed relationship graph intact while weakening the documentary reconstruction of booking.
design.scenario: The scheduled work combines a post-transfer holdings reconciliation and a review of current named provisions before further payments. The transfer file establishes a real movement but expressly limits its scope. The operative files establish a source-only relationship and an independently authorised relationship spanning both trusts; preserving both makes blanket migration and blanket suppression distinguishable.
shortcut_heuristics: Test merge-by-portfolio, inherit-the-roster, move-not-copy and suppress-all-overlap rules. Check exact trust names, local portfolio references and the chronology; a common custodian or transaction reference is not evidence of a shared trust identity.
Inspect headings, filenames, ordering and copied roster wording for a shortcut. A provider record and the reconciliation that uses it do not supply two independent relationship assertions.
success_criteria: Two isolated whole-file readers agree on the exact complete graph and on the distinction between shared beneficiaries and shared or transferred property. Fresh excerpt and deletion readers verify the sufficient subsets, the continuing edge on the other trust and the basis for restraint.

Stop if the actual transaction requires construing implied succession or external law, the supposedly independent designation in fact gives effect to the transfer, or the only way to make the record set work is to invent a second planning task or omit a controlling record.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and workflow integration 11–17; blind full-file and fresh excerpt or removal review 10–15; adjudication and audit 7–11; owner realism and readiness review 3–5. Assumes one completed transaction, two isolated complete reads and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 8 natural Sources. The two trusts' governance papers, executed transfer, separate provider advices, period reconciliation and briefing have distinct creators or business purposes.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse C's exact endpoint and invariant-graph audits, D's scope checks, and existing same-edge subsets and independently rederived review-only keys.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use exact Trust endpoints and beneficiary_of plus independently supported ordinary predicates. Asset movement, accounts, transfer powers and the inapplicability of a route stay in evidence or the companion register, not in new nodes or edges.
risks_and_limits: This is one natural case, not a causal estimate of the effect of adding transfer records or a claim about real trust succession.
If the transfer and designation would ordinarily be documented as one operative act, or the independent overlap lacks its own business reason, defer rather than manufacture separation.

assumptions: The supplied instruments expressly establish the separate continuing trusts, the limited effect of the transfer and the independently effective receiving-trust designation. The designation is not conditional on movement or evidence of movement; no legal consequences of asset tracing, resettlement or validity need be inferred.

The separate designation serves an actual planning purpose in the receiving trust and was made independently of the transfer paperwork, not added as a benchmark control. Both provider advices and the reconciliation serve actual closing checks.

Freeze after both the designation and the booked transfer, when the adviser has both providers' confirmations and the reconciliation for the upcoming review. Include any controlling current provisions normally available then.
grounding.documentary_situation: Two existing settlements remain in operation after a partial transfer. The transfer instrument limits the transaction to specified assets and does not adopt the source trust's provisions. In separately retained governance work, the receiving trust has expressly added one person who also remains a named beneficiary of the source trust. Another named source-trust beneficiary is not added by the supplied decisions. The portfolio records reconcile the same actual transfer without being evidence of beneficiary designations.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile a partial in-specie movement between two continuing settlements and review their current provisions before the next accounting and payment cycle.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Confirm what moved between the accounts and brief separately on the named relationships supported for each trust at the cut-off.
practitioner_unknowns: Would a partial in-specie movement and an independent designation naturally be reviewed together without a single closing record that conflates them or conclusively restates the entire roster?
Would both continuing trusts' provisions and both provider records be available to this adviser by the proposed review without obtaining extra material solely for the comparison?

references.relevance: Grounds the retention of investment information, instruments, decisions and accounts supporting the separate governance and reconciliation workstreams. It does not establish the power to move assets or the effect on named provisions.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Post-transfer advice on two settlements whose asset and beneficiary records must remain distinct.

objective.coverage_gap: C selects which one of two trusts a single designation concerns. It cannot diagnose whether real asset movement between two already identified, continuing trusts propagates their relationships or whether an overlap has independent authority. S varies the use of a list in one decision; BG has no ambiguous list function, and both the separate receiving designation and the asset transfer are genuine completed acts.
objective.failure_mechanism: A system may move all source-trust beneficiaries with the property, merge the trusts, suppress the independently supported overlapping beneficiary, or cite an asset entry for an otherwise correct named edge.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: On the complete file, named relationships remain attached to the trust whose operative records support them. A person can be supported in both trusts by separate provisions, while an actual transfer is insufficient to add another person to the receiving roster. Exact graph recovery and sufficient same-edge proof disconfirm the predicted errors on this file.

proposals.title: Moving assets does not move the named relationships

stopping_criteria: Before authoring, justify every proposed Source by its creator, contemporaneous business purpose, custody and availability at one freeze cut-off. Stop rather than pad the inventory, suppress an ordinarily retained controlling record, invent a routing convention or require unseen evidence.

Do not lock a file unless two isolated whole-file readers independently reconstruct the complete graph, discrepancies are adjudicated, and fresh readers verify exact support and the reason for each focal omission. Confirm exact passage attribution and attachment on the same edge; an acceptable singleton needs no redundant citation.

For each necessary-component diagnostic, remove copies of the fact as well as the focal passage and independently rederive the whole key. Credit surviving sufficient alternatives. If they make the proposed distinction dispensable, return the design; do not redefine necessity or treat an unresolved edge as denied.

Stop if the result needs an ontology extension, a scoring change, outside legal adjudication, retrieval, OCR or a stitched section-only key. Do not commission held-out, sealed or giant work. Human admission and any separate workload-tier decision remain outside this plan.
